issues.t: Air suspension sags or compressor runs nonstop
issues.sym: One corner or the whole rear sits low after parking, the ride turns harsh, a "check suspension" message appears, or you hear the air compressor running for long stretches.
issues.why: The rubber air springs dry out and crack with age, so they leak. The compressor then works overtime to keep up and eventually burns out, and the air dryer can clog.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks before replacing the compressor, or the new one will fail too. Switch the air suspension off before jacking the vehicle. Many owners convert to coil springs to save money.

issues.t: Cam phaser and timing chain knock
issues.sym: A ticking or diesel-like knock at idle, rough running, and a check engine light, often with camshaft timing codes.
issues.why: The 3-valve 5.4L uses oil-pressure-driven cam phasers and long timing chains. The phasers wear and stick, and the chain tensioners and guides wear, especially when oil changes are skipped.
issues.next: Have the timing codes read and oil pressure checked. Use the correct oil and change it on time. If the knock is loud, do not keep driving it hard, because a jumped chain can damage the engine.

issues.t: Spark plug blown out of the cylinder head
issues.sym: A sudden loud ticking or popping from one side of the engine, a misfire, loss of power, and a check engine light. The coil may be pushed up out of its hole.
issues.why: The aluminum cylinder heads on these 5.4L engines have only a few threads holding each spark plug. Over time the threads loosen and the plug can shoot out.
issues.next: Stop driving as soon as it is safe. A shop can usually install a thread insert without removing the head. Have the other plugs checked for correct torque too.

issues.t: Spark plugs break off during replacement
issues.sym: Usually found during a tune-up: the shop calls to say a plug snapped in the head. Before that you may notice a misfire and a check engine light.
issues.why: The early 3-valve 5.4L uses a two-piece spark plug whose lower shell sticks in carbon and breaks off when removed.
issues.next: Use a shop that knows this engine and has the special extraction tool. Ask for an estimate per broken plug before the job starts.

issues.t: Power running boards stick or stop deploying
issues.sym: The power running boards stay out, stay in, deploy on one side only, or grind and click when the doors open.
issues.why: The motors and hinges sit under the vehicle where road salt and water get in. They rust, the motors fail, and the linkages seize.
issues.next: Have both motors and the linkages checked. Cleaning and greasing the hinges sometimes frees them; otherwise the motor on the failed side is replaced.

issues.t: Rear liftgate glass shatters
issues.sym: The rear flip-up window breaks on its own, often when the liftgate or the glass is closed.
issues.why: Stress on the rear glass at its hinges and latch points can make it crack and shatter without an impact.
issues.next: Cover the opening and have the glass replaced. Ask the glass shop to check the hinges and latch so the new glass is not stressed.

issues.t: Air suspension warning light with no real fault
issues.sym: The air suspension warning lamp comes on even though the ride height looks normal.
issues.why: On early Navigators the air suspension control module could set the warning by mistake. A new module was the fix.
issues.next: Have the air suspension codes read to rule out a real leak first. If the system checks out, the control module is the likely cause.

issues.t: Throttle sticks on cold mornings
issues.sym: In very cold weather the gas pedal feels stuck or the engine is hard to start and run smoothly right after a cold start.
issues.why: Moisture from the crankcase ventilation (PCV) system can freeze around the throttle. Ford released a PCV service kit for these years.
issues.next: Have a Lincoln dealer or shop check for the PCV kit. Until then, do not force the pedal; let the engine warm up first.

issues.t: Power accessories stop working after the key is off
issues.sym: Windows, radio and other accessories do not work for the usual short time after you turn the key off.
issues.why: The battery saver relay that keeps accessory power on for a while after shutdown can fail.
issues.next: Have the relay tested and replaced. It is a cheap part and not a safety issue.

issues.t: Harsh or erratic 10-speed shifts
issues.sym: Hard clunks between gears, jerky downshifts when slowing down, or the transmission hunting between gears.
issues.why: The 10-speed automatic relies on learned shift settings, and early software caused rough shifts on many Ford and Lincoln trucks. Software updates and, in some cases, valve body work are the fixes.
issues.next: Ask a Lincoln dealer to check for software updates and reset the shift learning. If it slips or bangs hard, have it diagnosed before the damage spreads.

issues.t: Center touchscreen freezes or goes black
issues.sym: The SYNC touchscreen freezes, reboots, or goes blank, taking the radio, navigation and phone features with it.
issues.why: Software faults in the infotainment system. Updates have been released to fix many of these problems.
issues.next: Check that the system software is up to date. A dealer can do a master reset or reflash before replacing any module.

issues.t: Cruise control deactivation switch can catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some owners notice a burning smell or smoke near the brake master cylinder, even with the engine off.
issues.why: The switch that cancels cruise control when you brake can leak brake fluid internally and overheat.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 05V-388 and 05V-017. If the fix was never done, park outside and away from buildings until it is.

issues.t: Wiper motor switch can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers stop working, or you notice a burning smell near the base of the windshield.
issues.why: A switch inside the wiper motor gear case can overheat, which can kill the wipers or start a fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 01V-258 and have the wiper motor repaired.

issues.t: Park may not engage (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle can roll after you shift into Park and let off the brake.
issues.why: A guide plate for the parking pawl inside the transmission may be defective, so Park does not lock.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 05V-519. Always set the parking brake until the repair is done.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can leak into the booster (recalls)
issues.sym: A low brake fluid warning, a brake pedal that travels farther than normal, or longer stops.
issues.why: Brake fluid can leak from the master cylinder into the brake booster, cutting braking power.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 22V-150 and 25V-236. Any change in pedal feel needs a check before more driving.

issues.t: Front blower motor can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The fan speed changes or stops, or there is a hot or burning smell from the passenger footwell.
issues.why: The front blower motor can seize or short and overheat, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-648. Turn the fan off and have it inspected if you smell burning.

issues.t: Backup camera image distorted or blank (recalls)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture is blank, flipped, or distorted when you shift into Reverse.
issues.why: A loose or damaged connector or wiring in the camera circuit.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 25V-572 and 25V-270 and look around the vehicle when backing up until it is fixed.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell, sometimes with a check engine light or rough running.
issues.why: Welds on the engine-mounted high-pressure fuel pump can crack and leak fuel near hot engine parts.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V-392. If you smell fuel, park outside and have it inspected before driving.

issues.t: Park pawl can engage while moving (recall)
issues.sym: A loud bang or grinding and a sudden jolt while driving, or the vehicle not holding in Park afterwards.
issues.why: The parking pawl inside the transmission can drop in while the vehicle is moving, damaging the park system.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-402. Use the parking brake every time you park until the repair is done.

issues.t: Front seat belt can lock in place (recalls)
issues.sym: A front seat belt suddenly locks tight and will not pull out or retract.
issues.why: The seat belt pretensioner can fire or lock the belt without a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 24V-099, 25V-197 and 26V-344. A locked belt cannot protect you properly, so have it replaced soon.

issues.t: Instrument cluster can go blank (recalls)
issues.sym: The gauge cluster stays dark at startup, so speed, fuel level and warning lights are not shown.
issues.why: A software problem in the instrument cluster. An earlier repair was not always done correctly, so a second recall was issued.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 19V-076 and 26V-372, even if the first repair was done.

issues.t: Rear toe link bolts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear over bumps, or the vehicle pulling or wandering.
issues.why: Fasteners on the rear toe links may not have been tightened properly and can loosen or come apart.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V-773. A loose rear link affects steering control, so have it checked soon.

issues.t: Battery junction box can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning before a fire. Some owners notice electrical faults or a burning smell.
issues.why: The battery junction box under the hood can short circuit and overheat, even when parked.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-628 and follow the advice to park outside until it is repaired.

issues.t: Backup camera blank, frozen or delayed (recalls)
issues.sym: The rear camera image does not appear, freezes, shows up late, or stays on the screen after leaving Reverse.
issues.why: Software errors and camera faults in the rear-view camera system.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 23V-598, 25V-442 and 25V-315, and look around the vehicle when backing up until it is fixed.

issues.t: Engine compartment fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a fire under the hood.
issues.why: A fault in the engine compartment can lead to a fire, so Ford told owners to park outside.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-346 and park outside, away from buildings, until it is repaired.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Hard starting, sputtering, loss of power, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank can fail.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-455. A stall at speed is a crash risk, so get it repaired promptly.

issues.t: Trailer brakes or lights may stop working (recalls)
issues.sym: A trailer warning message, and trailer brakes or lights that stop working while towing.
issues.why: The trailer module can lose communication or have a software error.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 22V-193, 25V-132 and 26V-104. Do not tow a heavy trailer until the repair is done.

issues.t: Front brake line can rub through and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A brake warning light, low brake fluid, a soft pedal, or fluid near the front of the engine bay.
issues.why: A front brake line can rub against the air cleaner pipe and wear through.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-314. Do not drive with a soft pedal or a brake warning light.

issues.t: Rear camera and driver aids can drop out (recall)
issues.sym: Warnings that driver-assist features are unavailable, and the rear camera image cutting out.
issues.why: The image processing module can reset itself, switching off the camera and driver-assist features for a time.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-165 and do not rely on the driver aids until the update is done.

issues.t: Front axle pinion can break (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or grinding from the front axle, or the vehicle rolling when parked without the parking brake set.
issues.why: Some front axle pinion gears were not heat-treated and can fracture.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V-128 and use the parking brake every time you park.

issues.t: Engine plug can let oil out fast (recalls)
issues.sym: An oil pressure warning, oil leaking under the vehicle, or engine noise.
issues.why: A cup plug in the engine may have been installed out of position and can push out, dumping oil quickly.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 24V-851 and 25V-198. If the oil pressure light comes on, stop and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Brake booster can lose power assist (recalls)
issues.sym: A brake warning, and a pedal that suddenly takes much more effort to stop the vehicle.
issues.why: The electronic brake booster can lose its power assist.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 25V-488 and 25V-823. Leave extra stopping distance until it is repaired.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may deploy too hard (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving; the risk shows up only in a crash.
issues.why: The front passenger airbag may inflate with more force than intended.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 25V-439 and have the repair done.

issues.t: Front passenger seat can move on its own (recall)
issues.sym: The front passenger seat moves forward or back without anyone pressing the switch.
issues.why: A fault in the rear audio module can send commands that move the front passenger seat.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-691 and keep hands and objects clear of the seat track until it is fixed.

issues.t: Driver seat can move unexpectedly at low speed (recall)
issues.sym: The driver seat shifts position on its own, for example while maneuvering slowly.
issues.why: Software for the seat obstacle-detection feature can move the driver seat when it should not.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-120 and have the software update done.
